The error was caused by R8 minification stripping generic type information (`Signature` attributes) and anonymous `TypeToken` subclasses during the release build. When `TypeToken<List<Book>>` was instantiated at runtime, Gson could not determine the type parameter from the stripped bytecode, throwing:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: TypeToken must be created with a type argument: new TypeToken<...>() {}; When using code shrinkers (ProGuard, R8, ...) make sure that generic signatures are preserved.
```

### Changes Made

Updated [app/proguard-rules.pro](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c4-agy-B-r5/work/app/proguard-rules.pro#L1-L15) with the following rules:

```pro
# Project-specific R8 rules. The default rules come from proguard-android-optimize.txt.

# Preserve generic signatures and annotations for Gson reflection and TypeToken
-keepattributes Signature
-keepattributes *Annotation*

# Keep Gson's TypeToken class and all subclasses/anonymous implementations
-keep class com.google.gson.reflect.TypeToken { *; }
-keep class * extends com.google.gson.reflect.TypeToken
-keepclassmembers class * extends com.google.gson.reflect.TypeToken {
    <init>();
}

# Keep model classes so Gson can deserialize fields properly
-keep class vn.shelftap.lab.model.** { *; }
```

These rules:
1. Preserve the `Signature` attribute so Gson can inspect the generic type argument at runtime.
2. Prevent R8 from removing or inlining `TypeToken` and anonymous subclasses extending it.
3. Keep the model classes in `vn.shelftap.lab.model` intact so Gson can map JSON keys to fields correctly.
